verdict.rationale: SvelteKit server-renders routes by default and names a first-party `adapter-vercel` for deploying to a serverless host, with ISR support. A community user also reports running SvelteKit happily on Netlify. However, the pack never documents the general adapter system, edge-runtime targets, or a zero-config deploy flow, so most of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit docs on serverless/edge adapters (e.g. Cloudflare, Netlify, edge functions), an evidenced zero-config deployment workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration of edge deployment.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy my server-rendered app to serverless or edge runtimes without custom infrastructure setup

citations.quote: you can avoid long build times with Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) if using `adapter-vercel`
These will be server-rendered so that a user's first visit to your app is as fast as possible
